quantity: byte -> observed attack time, from audio. t_peak is time from note-on to the envelope's peak (the full 0->100 traversal); rise_10_90 is the 10-90% rise. BOTH are given because 'attack time' is ambiguous between them and the difference is a factor of ~1.6.
method: one preset with steady material, Atk1 rate written over SysEx, note held and the rise measured from the recorded audio. Per-point hold and window: window ~5% of the expected rise floored at 20 ms, hold ~6x the expected time. A fixed window cannot measure a ladder spanning 0.1-12 s and a fixed hold truncates the top. MATERIAL NOT IDENTIFIED -- see RESOLUTION_NOTES 111. 'One preset with steady material' names no preset and no sample, so this ladder cannot be re-taken or extended on the material it was measured on. It was written as a standalone result and has since become a cross-machine reference, which is a load it was not documented for. Verified-steady material has since been established by measurement (amp envelope flattened to a rectangle, sample contour read directly): E4XT RAM preset P007 as loaded 2026-09-11 gives 0.22-0.71 dB of ripple over 6 s on notes 52/65/79. Use that, or re-establish the same way, for any extension.

shape_ratio.note: measured on the E4XT itself. A sibling project's 0.704 is the MPC One's figure; the machines have different ramp shapes and the difference propagates into any converted time.
shape_ratio.scope: 0.619 is measured on one preset. RESOLUTION_NOTES 119: the analogous ratio varies 7.6% between programs on a sibling machine, so treat this as a one-preset figure with unmeasured spread, not a machine constant.

range_limit: NOT to be read below ~2 s without a re-take. The three sub-second points drift (see flags/ratios); at byte 48 the 30 ms window is only ~3.5% of the rise, so quantisation is a real fraction of the measurement.
cross_check: a preset whose panel showed Atk1 rate 89 measured t_peak ~10.1 s; byte 89 on a different preset with different material gave 9.10 s. The timing follows the byte across programs, which a material artefact could not. SCOPE CORRECTION 2026-09-14 (RESOLUTION_NOTES 119): the two figures differ by 11.0%, and that was recorded as agreement. A sibling project has since shown the same envelope byte giving a 33% different attack AND a different shape between two programs of one machine, with every readable envelope parameter identical or ruled out. So 11% is the size of a real program-dependent effect, not only noise. The cross-check shows the BYTE IS THE MAIN TERM (9.1 s at byte 89 against 0.18 s at byte 20); it does NOT show the byte is the only term, which is what it has been cited for.
interpolation: ln(t_peak) is near-linear in byte: slope 0.0525-0.0656 per byte across all seven intervals. USE LOG INTERPOLATION. Linear interpolation over the widest gap (87->96) differs by 0.4 s: byte 91 gives 11.63 s linear against 11.22 s log-linear. The rule was unstated once and the two models were quoted interchangeably -- see RESOLUTION_NOTES §105 addendum.

additional_points.provenance: measured on a DIFFERENT bank and different material from the ladder rows, with a separate script. Recorded because it sits inside the ladder's widest gap (87->96), but NOT merged into rows: this ladder's own cross-program check found byte 89 giving 10.1 s on one preset and 9.10 s on another, ~11%, so points from different material are not interchangeable with the rows.

scope: SEG0 (Atk1) ONLY, and SEG0 is not the whole attack on presets that use two attack segments. An envelope whose Atk1 LEVEL is below 100% continues rising through Atk2, so t_peak is at the end of SEG1 and this table does not predict it. Combine as 1.838 * (R(atk1) * L1 + R(atk2) * (1 - L1)) with L1 = Atk1 level. Reading this table against a two-segment attack understates it by up to 5x -- measured: byte 39 interpolates to 0.58 s against a 2.92 s measured t_peak on a preset whose Atk1 level is 43%.
detector: ARGMAX of a 5 ms-smoothed envelope, which is NOT the convention this project settled on 2026-09-11 (5 ms smoothing / threshold-crossing / -3.0 dB of the plateau reference). The two families differ by 1.89x on the SAME steady material: byte 72 reads 3.849 s by argmax and 2.035 s by threshold. So every t_peak in `rows` is an argmax figure and must not be compared against a threshold figure. See RESOLUTION_NOTES 113: on a convex rise there is no knee, so the two families measure different points of the curve and MUST disagree by an amount set by the curvature.
superseded_note: A sibling project withdrew a derived constant (`_E4XT_ATK_SLOWDOWN = 1.838`) built on this table, on the grounds that the 1.8x was a detector artefact rather than a machine property. THAT CONCLUSION IS SUPPORTED HERE; THE STATED MECHANISM IS NOT. They attribute it to this ladder's DECAYING material biasing t_peak LATE. Measured on steady material at the same detector, byte 72 reads 3.849 s against this table's 3.600 -- so the decaying material biases t_peak EARLY by 7%, not late, which is the same sign RESOLUTION_NOTES 112 measured directly (-11% on a two-segment preset). The 1.8x is the DETECTOR FAMILY, not the material. The distinction matters because it says the fix is to state the convention, not to change the material.

row_schema_required.why: RESOLUTION_NOTES 120. The rows below carry byte and times but no preset, no note and no per-note level, and that blocked three separate retrospective tests within half an hour on 2026-09-14 -- a sample-rate test (needs preset), an uncontrolled-note reading (needs note) and a test locating the envelope's convexity (needs level per note). Each was a lookup in data already taken; none can be recovered without re-measuring on material no longer in RAM. 'velocity' added 2026-09-14: hold velocity fixed AND demonstrate the plateau is insensitive to it BY MEASUREMENT on the material actually used. Do not size the test against any borrowed number: a sibling machine showed 16.5 dB of plateau movement across velocity 40-127, but that is a property of one program with its velocity-to-level depth set to 20, NOT of that machine -- a program with the depth at 0 should show almost none. The magnitude is a property of the subject; only the instruction transfers. And the reason a parameter read cannot substitute: reading the velocity-to-ATTACK fields as 0 was CORRECT there; a velocity-to-LEVEL field in the same header was non-zero and unexamined. The failure is an incomplete enumeration of routes, not a wrong read -- a read tells you about the field you read and nothing about the one you did not think to.
row_schema_required.rule: Record every column on every row ALWAYS, including when no current question needs it. The cost of a missing column is never visible when you decide not to add it, and it is never paid by the session that omitted it.

DETECTOR_WARNING_2026_09_14: RESOLUTION_NOTES 121. This ladder's times were taken with a FIXED 5 ms detector on transposed material. A note ladder plays ONE sample at many rates, so the sample's own amplitude modulation is stretched by 2^((origkey-note)/12) and a fixed-timescale detector resolves a different number of sample-periods at every note. Measured live 2026-09-14 on identified single-zone material: a fixed 5 ms detector reports an attack ratio of 1.655x across 48 semitones, and the SAME captures measured with smoothing scaled to the playback rate report 0.962x -- flat. A no-attack control (instant attack, nothing to measure) reports 0.060 s at note 16 against 0.020 s at note 64 at fixed 5 ms. The rows below are single-note (the note is not recorded) so they are NOT affected across rungs, but any note-dependence derived from this method is suspect, including 113's 1.25x. Scale the detector with the playback rate, or measure at one note only.
